newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ekran says dam project can proceed.
newsitem.headline: Ekran says dam project can proceed.

text.p: Malaysia's Ekran Bhd said on Monday that its 13.6 billion ringgit ($5.5 billion) dam project will be able to proceed unhindered following an Appeals Court ruling in its favour on an environmental issue.
Speaking to reporters following the ruling earlier on Monday, Ekran executive chairman Ting Pek Khiing said, "The project can now go on very smoothly and it can put Malaysia on the world map."

The Appeals Court earlier on Monday said it dismissed without costs a High Court environmental ruling against Ekran, saying the Environmental Quality Act referred to by the High Court was not applicable in this case.
Three tribals affected by the massive dam, being built in the tropical jungles of Sarawak state on Borneo island, had sued to stop the project on environmental grounds.
A jubilant Ting said, "The EPC (engineering, procurement and construction) of the project can now go on full swing."
He said that while the High Court ruling had not prevented construction on the project, since the ruling was later suspended, "There should not be any more doubt on Bakun after the decision today."
Work on the dam began at the start of 1997 and Ting said the dam, which has a 2,400 megawatt capacity, should be completed as scheduled by January 2003 "or maybe a year earlier".
Ting said only preliminary work had been started on the project.

Asked about the plaintiffs' plan to appeal Monday's decision, Ekran's legal adviser Muhammad Shafee Abdullah said, "We made our appeal today in the same manner that we appealed against the High Court ruling...we'll stick to this same ground and maybe come out with a few more."
"Frankly, I see a little chance of anyone appealing and being successful," Muhammad Shafee told reporters.
Ting reiterated the company's view that it had abided by environmental laws in building the dam, which will flood an area the size of Singapore.
"As far as Ekran is concerned, we are following all conditions stipulated by the Sarawak government," he said.

Asked about expectations on the public share offering for Bakun Hydro-Electric Corp, the holding company for the dam, Ting said, "Profits made by Bakun will be more than enough for the public to invest."

Analysts said there have been concerns that the offering, which includes a public issue of 375 million shares, would receive only a lukewarm response partly due to the uncertainties about the returns from the project.
Ting responded: "Profits will come from day one. This is a very different kind of project, there's not much loan, not much interest to service."
"There is no other uncertainty in income," Ting added. "It's a big amount of power, and the amount will be fixed."
